shortQuestions.question: What are the key points an external auditor should review when relying on the work of an internal auditor?

items: Audit programs are adequate.
Work is performed by trained staff and assistants are properly supervised, reviewed and documented.
Sufficient appropriate audit evidence was obtained.
Conclusions made are appropriate.
Reports prepared are based on the work done.
Exceptions or unusual items have been properly resolved.

shortQuestions.question: List the methods an external auditor can use to test the work of internal auditing.

items: Re-performing the work done by internal auditor, on test basis, to ensure that the same results are achieved.
Selecting a few similar items and performing independent tests.
Observation of internal auditing procedures.

shortQuestions.question: Define an Audit Engagement Letter and state its objective.

answerBlocks.text: An Audit Engagement Letter is a written document by the auditor to the client that records the terms of engagement as agreed between them.
Its objective is to confirm the acceptance and understanding of the audit engagement, including the scope, responsibilities, and other relevant terms.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the principal contents of an Audit Engagement Letter.

items: The objective of financial statements.
Management’s responsibility for financial statements.
The scope of the audit.
The form of any reports or other communications.
The fact that auditors may not detect all material misstatements due to fraud or error.
Requirement of unrestricted access to records.

shortQuestions.question: What optional contents may be included in an Audit Engagement Letter?

items: Arrangements regarding the planning of the audit.
Expectation of receiving written representations.
Request for confirmation of terms of engagement.
Description of any other letters or reports the auditor expects to issue to the client.
Basis for computation of fees.

shortQuestions.question: List the contents to be included under special circumstances in an Audit Engagement Letter.

items: Arrangements concerning the involvement of other auditors, experts, internal auditors and other client staff.
Arrangements to be made with predecessor auditor, in case of initial audit only.
Restriction on auditor’s liability, if any.
Reference to any further agreements between the auditor and the client.

shortQuestions.question: What factors determine whether a separate engagement letter is needed for auditing components such as branches or subsidiaries?

items: Who appoints the auditor of the component.
Whether a separate audit report is to be issued on the component.
Legal requirements.
The extent of any work performed by other auditors.
Degree of ownership by the parent company.
Degree of independence of the component’s management.

shortQuestions.question: When should an auditor write a new engagement letter for recurring audits?

items: If the client misunderstands the objective and scope of the audit.
Any revised or special terms of engagement.
A recent change of senior management, board of directors or ownership.
A significant change in nature or size of the client’s business.
Legal requirements.

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain the responsibilities of management as stated in the example Audit Engagement Letter.

answerBlocks.text: Management is responsible for the preparation of financial statements including adequate disclosure.
This includes maintaining adequate accounting records and internal controls, selecting and applying accounting policies, and safeguarding the company's assets.

shortQuestions.question: What does the example Audit Engagement Letter say about the auditor's fees?

answerBlocks.text: The fees will be billed as work progresses and are based on the time required by the individuals assigned to the engagement plus out-of-pocket expenses.
Individual hourly rates vary according to the degree of responsibility involved and the experience and skill required.

lessons.title: PLANNING AN AUDIT OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

shortQuestions.question: Define the purpose of planning an audit.

answerBlocks.text: The auditor should plan the audit so that the engagement will be performed in an effective manner. Planning an audit involves establishing the overall audit strategy for the engagement and developing an audit plan, in order to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level.

shortQuestions.question: List the benefits of adequate audit planning.

items: Ensure appropriate attention is devoted to important areas of the audit.
Identify and resolve potential problems on a timely basis.
Proper organization and management of the audit engagement.
Proper assignment of work to engagement team members.
Facilitate direction, supervision, and review of engagement team members' work.
Coordinate work done by auditors of components and experts.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the factors that affect the nature and extent of planning activities.

items: Size and complexity of the entity.
Auditor’s previous experience with the entity.
Changes in circumstances that occur during the audit engagement.

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain the overall audit strategy.

answerBlocks.text: The overall audit strategy sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit, and guides the development of the more detailed audit plan. It involves determining characteristics defining the engagement scope, ascertaining reporting objectives, and considering important factors that determine the focus of the engagement team's efforts.

shortQuestions.question: List the key elements considered in establishing the overall audit strategy.

items: Determining characteristics defining the engagement scope such as financial reporting framework, industry-specific requirements, and locations of components.
Ascertaining reporting objectives including deadlines and key communication dates.
Considering important factors like materiality levels, higher risk areas, material components, evaluation of internal control evidence, and recent relevant developments.

shortQuestions.question: What does the overall audit strategy set out clearly regarding resources?

items: Resources to deploy for specific audit areas, including experienced team members and experts.
Amount of resources to allocate to specific audit areas, such as team size and audit budget.
Timing of resource deployment, e.g., interim audit stage or key cut-off dates.
Management, direction and supervision of resources, including meetings, reviews, and quality control.

shortQuestions.question: Distinguish between the overall audit strategy and the audit plan.

answerBlocks.text: The overall audit strategy sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit and guides the development of the audit plan. The audit plan is more detailed, specifying the nature, timing, and extent of audit procedures to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level.

shortQuestions.question: What are the main components included in the audit plan?

items: Description of the nature, timing and extent of planned risk assessment procedures.
Description of the nature, timing and extent of planned further audit procedures at the assertion level for each material class of transactions, account balance, and disclosure.
Other audit procedures required to comply with ISAs, such as direct communication with the entity’s lawyers.

shortQuestions.question: Explain why planning is considered a continual process during an audit engagement.

answerBlocks.text: Planning begins shortly after the previous audit and continues until completion of the current audit engagement. It is updated and changed as necessary due to unexpected events, changes in conditions, or audit evidence obtained, requiring modification of the overall audit strategy and audit plan.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the factors that influence the nature, timing and extent of direction and supervision of engagement team members.

items: Size and complexity of the entity.
The area of audit.
Risks of material misstatement.
Capabilities and competence of personnel performing the audit work.

shortQuestions.question: What should the auditor document regarding the overall audit strategy and audit plan?

items: Key decisions necessary to properly plan the audit and communicate significant matters to the engagement team.
Planned nature, timing and extent of risk assessment procedures and further audit procedures at the assertion level.
Any significant changes made during the audit engagement including reasons and auditor’s response.
The final overall audit strategy and audit plan adopted for the audit.

shortQuestions.question: Give an example of when the auditor might significantly change the planned overall audit strategy and audit plan.

answerBlocks.text: The auditor may significantly change the planned overall audit strategy and audit plan as a result of a material business combination or the identification of a material misstatement of the financial statements.

lessons.title: Lesson 43

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain audit planning for small entities.

answerBlocks.text: In audits of small entities, the audit may be conducted by a very small team, often just the audit engagement partner or with one team member. Coordination and communication are easier, and establishing the overall audit strategy is less complex and time-consuming. A brief memorandum from the previous audit, updated with current discussions, can serve as the basis for planning.

shortQuestions.question: List the typical topics discussed with those charged with governance during audit planning.

items: The overall audit strategy and timing of the audit
Any limitations on the audit
Any additional requirements

shortQuestions.question: Outline additional considerations the auditor should perform before starting an initial audit engagement.

items: Perform procedures regarding acceptance of the client relationship and specific audit engagement.
Communicate with the previous auditor if there has been a change of auditors.
Consider arrangements to review previous auditor’s working papers, unless prohibited by law.
Consider major issues discussed with management related to initial auditor selection.
Plan audit procedures to obtain evidence on opening balances.
Assign personnel with appropriate capabilities to respond to significant risks.
Perform other quality control procedures required by the firm’s system.

shortQuestions.question: List examples of matters the auditor may consider in establishing the overall audit strategy.

items: Scope of the audit engagement
Reporting objectives
Direction of the audit

shortQuestions.question: What matters may the auditor consider when establishing the scope of the audit engagement?

items: Financial reporting framework and any need for reconciliations
Industry-specific reporting requirements
Expected audit coverage including components and locations
Control relationships between parent and components
Extent of audit by other auditors
Nature of business segments and need for specialized knowledge
Reporting currency and currency translation needs
Need for statutory audit of standalone financial statements
Availability and reliance on internal auditors’ work
Use of service organizations and controls performed by them
Use of prior audit evidence
Effect of information technology and computer-assisted audit techniques
Coordination with interim financial information reviews
Discussions with firm personnel performing other services
Availability of client personnel and data

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain matters to consider regarding reporting objectives, timing, and communications in audit planning.

items: Entity’s timetable for interim and final reporting
Organization of meetings with management and those charged with governance
Expected type and timing of reports and communications including auditor’s report and management letters
Communications on audit status and expected deliverables
Communication with auditors of components about reports and timing
Nature and timing of engagement team communications and meetings
Any other expected communications with third parties

shortQuestions.question: What factors does the auditor consider when setting the direction of the audit related to materiality?

items: Setting materiality for planning purposes
Setting and communicating materiality for auditors of components
Reconsidering materiality during audit procedures
Identifying material components and account balances
Audit areas with higher risk of material misstatement
Impact of assessed risks on direction, supervision, and review

shortQuestions.question: List considerations for the selection and assignment of the engagement team during audit planning.

items: Selecting engagement team members including quality control reviewer if necessary
Assigning audit work to team members with appropriate experience
Assigning experienced members to areas with higher risks of material misstatement

shortQuestions.question: Outline factors influencing engagement budgeting in audit planning.

answerBlocks.text: Engagement budgeting involves considering the appropriate amount of time to allocate for audit areas where there may be higher risks of material misstatement.

shortQuestions.question: Explain the importance of professional skepticism in audit planning.

answerBlocks.text: The auditor emphasizes to engagement team members the need to maintain a questioning mind and to exercise professional skepticism in gathering and evaluating audit evidence.

shortQuestions.question: What previous audit results may influence the audit planning process?

items: Results evaluating the operating effectiveness of internal control
Nature of identified weaknesses and actions taken to address them

shortQuestions.question: List significant developments the auditor may consider when establishing the overall audit strategy.

items: Significant business developments such as changes in IT, business processes, key management, acquisitions, mergers, and divestments
Significant industry developments including regulatory changes and new reporting requirements
Significant changes in the financial reporting framework like accounting standards
Other relevant developments such as changes in the legal environment affecting the entity

lessons.title: AUDITOR’S REPORT ON A COMPLETE SET OF GENERAL PURPOSE FINANCIALSTATEMENTS

shortQuestions.question: Define the auditor’s report on a complete set of general purpose financial statements.

answerBlocks.text: An auditor’s report is issued as a result of an audit of a complete set of general purpose financial statements prepared in accordance with a financial reporting framework designed to achieve fair presentation. It contains a clear expression of the auditor’s opinion on the financial statements.

shortQuestions.question: List the phrases used to express the auditor’s opinion on financial statements and explain their equivalence.

items: "Give a true and fair view"
"Are presented fairly, in all material respects"

answerBlocks.text: These phrases are equivalent and the choice of which to use depends on the law, regulations, or established practice in the jurisdiction.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the key considerations an auditor evaluates when forming an opinion on the financial statements.

items: Whether the accounting policies selected and applied are consistent with the financial reporting framework and appropriate in the circumstances.
Whether the accounting estimates made by management are reasonable.
Whether the information presented is relevant, reliable, comparable, and understandable.
Whether the financial statements provide sufficient disclosures to enable users to understand material transactions and events.

shortQuestions.question: List the elements of the auditor’s report when the audit is conducted in accordance with the ISAs.

items: Title
Addressee
Introductory paragraph
Management’s responsibility for the financial statements
Auditor’s responsibility
Auditor’s opinion
Other reporting responsibilities
Auditor’s signature
Date of the auditor’s report
Auditor’s address

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain the importance of the title in the auditor’s report.

answerBlocks.text: The title should clearly indicate that the report is from an independent auditor, such as "Independent Auditor’s Report." This affirms that the auditor has met ethical requirements regarding independence and distinguishes the report from others.

shortQuestions.question: What information should the introductory paragraph of the auditor’s report contain?

items: Identification of the entity whose financial statements have been audited.
A statement that the financial statements have been audited.
The title of each financial statement comprising the complete set.
Reference to the summary of significant accounting policies and other explanatory notes.
Specification of the date and period covered by the financial statements.

shortQuestions.question: Outline management’s responsibilities as stated in the auditor’s report.

items: Preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.
Designing, implementing, and maintaining internal control relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of financial statements free from material misstatement.
Selecting and applying appropriate accounting policies.
Making reasonable accounting estimates.

shortQuestions.question: Explain the auditor’s responsibilities as described in the auditor’s report.

items: Express an opinion on the financial statements based on the audit.
Conduct the audit in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISAs).
Comply with ethical requirements.
Plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement.
Perform procedures to obtain audit evidence about amounts and disclosures.
Use auditor’s judgment to select procedures based on risk assessments.
Evaluate the appropriateness of accounting policies, reasonableness of estimates, and overall presentation.

shortQuestions.question: When should an unqualified auditor’s opinion be expressed?

answerBlocks.text: An unqualified opinion should be expressed when the auditor concludes that the financial statements give a true and fair view or are presented fairly, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

shortQuestions.question: What additional reporting responsibilities might an auditor have in some jurisdictions?

answerBlocks.text: In some jurisdictions, the auditor may have additional responsibilities to report on other matters supplementary to the opinion on the financial statements, such as reporting certain matters that come to attention during the audit, performing additional specified procedures, or expressing opinions on specific matters like adequacy of accounting books and records.

shortQuestions.question: Describe the requirements for the date of the auditor’s report.

answerBlocks.text: The auditor should date the report no earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate audit evidence has been obtained to base the opinion. This evidence includes confirmation that the complete set of financial statements has been prepared and those with recognized authority have taken responsibility for them.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the format of the auditor’s report under the Companies Ordinance, 1984.

items: Introductory Paragraph stating the audit of balance sheet and related statements.
Management’s Responsibility for internal control and preparation of statements.
Auditor’s Responsibility describing the audit conducted according to applicable standards.
Opinion paragraph covering conformity with the Companies Ordinance, accounting policies, and true and fair view.
Other Responsibilities such as Zakat deduction and deposit.
Auditor’s Signature, Date, and Place.

lessons.title: DEPENDS UPON NATURE OF CIRCUMSTANCES

shortQuestions.question: Define a modified auditor's report.

answerBlocks.text: A modified auditor’s report is an auditor’s report whose wording is changed due to certain circumstances affecting the auditor’s opinion. These modifications occur when matters affect or do not affect the auditor’s opinion, such as qualified opinions, disclaimers, adverse opinions, or emphasis of matter paragraphs.

shortQuestions.question: List the three types of opinions that affect the auditor’s opinion in a modified report.

items: Qualified opinion
Disclaimer of opinion
Adverse opinion

shortQuestions.question: Briefly explain what is meant by a 'limitation on scope' in auditing.

answerBlocks.text: A limitation on scope occurs when the auditor is unable to carry out an audit procedure believed necessary, either due to restrictions imposed by the entity or circumstances such as timing or inadequate accounting records, which limits the auditor’s ability to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence.

shortQuestions.question: Outline the difference between a qualified opinion and a disclaimer of opinion due to limitation on scope.

answerBlocks.text: A qualified opinion is expressed when the limitation on scope is material but not pervasive, allowing the auditor to state an opinion 'except for' the effects of the limitation. A disclaimer of opinion is expressed when the limitation is so material and pervasive that the auditor cannot obtain sufficient evidence and thus cannot express any opinion.

shortQuestions.question: Distinguish between disagreements with management that lead to a qualified opinion and those that lead to an adverse opinion.

answerBlocks.text: A qualified opinion is expressed when the disagreement with management is material but not pervasive, allowing the auditor to qualify the opinion 'except for' the disagreement. An adverse opinion is expressed when the disagreement is so material and pervasive that a qualification is inadequate to disclose the misleading or incomplete nature of the financial statements.

shortQuestions.question: What is an emphasis of matter paragraph and when is it used?

answerBlocks.text: An emphasis of matter paragraph is added to the auditor’s report to highlight a matter affecting the financial statements that is disclosed in a note but does not affect the auditor’s opinion. It is used to draw attention to significant uncertainties or going concern problems without qualifying the opinion.

shortQuestions.question: List two examples of matters that do not affect the auditor’s opinion but may require an emphasis of matter paragraph.

items: Going concern problems
Significant uncertainties dependent on future events

shortQuestions.question: Explain the auditor’s responsibility when there is a limitation on scope imposed by the entity.

answerBlocks.text: When a limitation on scope is imposed by the entity, the auditor should evaluate whether the limitation requires a disclaimer of opinion. The auditor would ordinarily not accept an audit engagement with such a limitation unless required by statute, and a statutory auditor would not accept it if it infringes on statutory duties.

shortQuestions.question: What should the auditor’s report include when expressing an opinion other than unqualified?

items: A clear description of all substantive reasons for the modification
A quantification of possible effects on the financial statements, unless impracticable
This information is usually in a separate paragraph preceding the opinion or disclaimer

shortQuestions.question: Outline the auditor’s approach when a disagreement with management involves inadequate disclosure in the financial statements.

answerBlocks.text: If the disagreement involves inadequate disclosure and is material and pervasive, the auditor should express an adverse opinion stating that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view due to the effects of the disagreement.

shortQuestions.question: Where in the auditor’s report is an emphasis of matter paragraph preferably included?

answerBlocks.text: An emphasis of matter paragraph is preferably included after the paragraph containing the auditor’s opinion but before any section on other reporting responsibilities.

shortQuestions.question: When might an auditor consider expressing a disclaimer of opinion instead of adding an emphasis of matter paragraph for uncertainties?

answerBlocks.text: In extreme cases involving multiple significant uncertainties affecting the financial statements, the auditor may consider expressing a disclaimer of opinion instead of adding an emphasis of matter paragraph.
